Phase 1 · Two-part working checklist

Frame the Mandate

Two parts: macroeconomic analysis, then client submissions.

Part 1Macroeconomic AnalysisBuild and submit one documented 12-month macro forecast with three probability-weighted scenarios before applying it to the clients. Part 2Client SubmissionsUse the submitted macro forecast and each assigned client profile to produce IPS documents, a committee mandate, and a recorded Gate 1 decision in a separate client-analysis submission.

Decision question

What must be true about markets and each client before we are willing to invest?

Establish one defensible 12-month market view and convert each assigned client profile into an approved investment mandate.

Submit the macro forecast as Assignment 1. Use that forecast in Assignment 2 for the client analysis and Gate 1 vote. Each assignment has its own Canvas receipt.

Part 1 of 2

Macroeconomic Analysis

Build and submit one documented 12-month macro forecast with three probability-weighted scenarios before applying it to the clients.

Do this in order

  1. 1

    Open the Macro Starter workbook, assign all five roles, and save a team-named Part 1 copy.

  2. 2

    Complete the detailed macro analysis in the provided workbook: review historical evidence, form a human-first interpretation, and document sources.

  3. 3

    Compare the committee view with FRED historical observations and a source-dated FactSet or other external forecast or consensus where a comparable measure exists; then create bull, base, and bear scenarios with probabilities totaling 100%.

Ready when

  • The macro workbook documents historical analysis, source-dated external comparisons, inflation expectations, and weighted bull, base, and bear scenarios.

Evidence to keep

  • Human-first five-year macro read with source dates
  • Source-dated external forecast comparison, FRED historical evidence, and team growth, inflation, rate, and sentiment forecasts
  • Bull/base/bear scenarios with probabilities totaling 100%

Macro forecast deliverable

  • Completed macro starter workbook

Resources for this part

HTML Macro Forecast step-by-step guide Workbook-mapped steps for a human-first macro view, AI challenge, independent verification, scenarios, and the Part 1 submission. XLSX Macro starter workbook Source-dated historical data, human-first analysis, verified external comparisons, inflation expectations, and weighted bull/base/bear forecasts.

Assignment 1: submit the macro forecast

Complete and submit the macro starter workbook as the Part 1 group assignment. One designated team member submits for the group; every team member verifies the Canvas receipt. Carry the submitted forecast into Part 2 and document any later revision in the decision record.

  • BUS331_[TeamName]_Phase1_Macro.xlsxCompleted macro starter workbook with historical evidence, human-first read, source-dated consensus comparison, inflation forecast, and probability-weighted bull/base/bear scenarios.
Check this Canvas submission

Part 2 of 2

Client Submissions

Use the submitted macro forecast and each assigned client profile to produce IPS documents, a committee mandate, and a recorded Gate 1 decision in a separate client-analysis submission.

Do this in order

  1. 1

    Open the separate Decision Record, identify assigned clients, and analyze their scenario profiles and data. Separate supplied facts, reasoned assumptions, and information gaps.

  2. 2

    Translate the macro outlook into a client-specific IPS mandate, including return target, risk limit, drawdown tripwire, and provisional strategic allocation.

  3. 3

    Hold Gate 1: challenge the evidence, vote, and record required revisions before any portfolio construction begins.

Work from the assigned scenarios

Use the Client Scenario Analysis and Decision Protocol to separate stated facts, reasoned assumptions, and information gaps before finalizing each IPS.

Ready when

  • Each client has objectives, RRTTLLU constraints, a return target, risk limit, drawdown tripwire, provisional strategic allocation, and identified information gaps.
  • The committee can explain how its macro outlook changes each client mandate.
  • Each team member has recorded one Gate 1 vote and any revision actions; all five role responsibilities are covered.

Evidence to keep

  • RRTTLLU analysis for all three assigned clients
  • Return target, maximum volatility, and drawdown tripwire for each client
  • Provisional strategic allocation totaling 100% and a policy-level implementation plan for each client
  • Analyst Decision Log showing initial judgment, committee challenge, verification, final reasoning, and downstream guardrail
  • Phase 1 decision record showing every team member's vote, with all five roles covered

Client and committee deliverables

  • Completed Analyst Decision Log for all three assigned clients
  • Three completed client IPS documents
  • One-page committee mandate memo
  • Phase 1 decision record

Assignment 2: submit client analysis after Gate 1

Complete each IPS from the assigned fictional scenario, using labeled and justified assumptions for missing details; no client interviews are required. Use the macro forecast already submitted in Part 1; do not upload it again. After the Gate 1 vote, submit the three client-analysis files as the Part 2 group assignment. One designated team member submits for the group; every team member verifies the Canvas receipt.

Committee responsibilities across both parts

Committee seatResponsibility in Phase 1
Client and Macro StrategistLead analysis of the assigned client scenarios, document goals and RRTTLLU constraints, establish the macro context, and label reasoned assumptions and information gaps.
Fixed-Income AnalystTranslate cash-flow needs, time horizon, liquidity, taxes, and loss capacity into fixed-income questions and provisional guardrails.
Equity AnalystTranslate the client's growth needs, time horizon, values, tax position, liquidity, and concentration limits into equity-selection guardrails.
Portfolio ManagerReconcile risk capacity and willingness, set provisional portfolio guardrails, coordinate the committee challenge, and audit the Analyst Decision Log.
Risk and Derivatives AnalystDefine the downside questions, drawdown tripwire, stress priorities, and residual-risk evidence the final portfolio must address.

Gate 1 approval standard

Committee motion

Motion to approve the committee's market view and the investment mandate for each assigned client.

Approve or revise the common market view and all three client mandates. Portfolio construction cannot begin until the vote and action items are recorded.

The decision record must state the motion, evidence reviewed, each member's vote, any dissent or reservation, and the owner and due date for every required revision.
